evidence.passage: The final diagnosis was dyspnea due to congestive heart failure in 744 patients (47 percent), dyspnea due to noncardiac causes in 72 patients with a history of left ventricular dysfunction (5 percent), and no finding of congestive heart failure in 770 patients (49 percent).
evidence.reason: It reports the proportion of emergency department patients with acute dyspnea whose final diagnosis was congestive heart failure (present, 47%), though not restricted to ages 65+.
limitations: All-adult population, not restricted to age 65+
Outcome is congestive heart failure rather than specifically acute decompensated heart failure
Mean age and age-specific prevalence not given in the abstract

evidence.passage: The main causes of ARF were cardiogenic pulmonary edema (43%), community-acquired pneumonia (35%), acute exacerbation of chronic respiratory disease (32%), pulmonary embolism (18%), and acute asthma (3%); 47% had more than two diagnoses.
evidence.reason: It reports that pulmonary embolism was a cause in 18% of elderly emergency patients with acute dyspnea and respiratory failure, which is the prevalence of PE when the finding is present.
